content.text:
We need answer in JSON schema. Need extract claims from review. Need follow taxonomy. Source text: "Stopped working after a couple months\nStopped working after just 3 months. It was overheating very bad and when I contacted the seller he told me that he cannot do anything about it. Don’t recommend"

Need extract product-review semantic claims. Zero/multiple. For every claim choose exactly one valid primary/secondary pair, independently polarity, evidence_span exact continuous substring from SOURCE_TEXT. Do not infer sentiment from star rating. Do not invent evidence/topics. If no supported product claim exists, empty list.

We need identify claims about product. There are:
- "Stopped working after just 3 months" => reliability_durability / stopped_working, negative. Evidence exact substring maybe "Stopped working after just 3 months" or includes title? Source_text includes title at beginning: "Stopped working after a couple months\nStopped working after just 3 months..." We can use exact continuous substring. The claim "Stopped working after a couple months" also reliability/stopped_working negative. But same product? Title and first sentence. We need maybe one or two? It says review may contain zero/multiple claims. Each claim maybe independent. "Stopped working after a couple months" and "Stopped working after just 3 months" are similar but repeated. Could extract both? But they overlap semantically same claim. Usually should extract distinct claims. The title says stopped working after a couple months, then body says after just 3 months. Could be same claim. We can choose one evidence span. Maybe "Stopped working after just 3 months" as stronger. But title also exact. Need avoid duplicate? The schema doesn't forbid duplicate but quality. We'll likely include one stopped_working claim.

- "It was overheating very bad" => safety_risk / overheating, negative. Evidence "It was overheating very bad" exact substring. Is overheating safety risk. Polarity negative. Primary safety_risk secondary overheating.

- Seller response: "when I contacted the seller he told me that he cannot do anything about it." That's not product claim? It's customer service, not taxonomy. Could be other_unknown? But taxonomy has no customer service. Should not extract because no supported product claim? It's about seller, not product. Don't include.

- "Don’t recommend" is general recommendation not specific product claim? Could be overall sentiment but not a semantic claim about product attribute. Probably not.

Need decide if "overheating" and "stopped working" are related? Separate claims. Maybe "overheating very bad" caused stopped working? But separate topics: safety_risk overheating; reliability stopped_working. Could also be electrical_fault? But explicitly overheating. Primary safety_risk / overheating.

Need ensure evidence_span exact substring. Source_text includes newline. Evidence can be "Stopped working after just 3 months" or "Stopped working after a couple months". If we include title, exact substring "Stopped working after a couple months" is in source_text. That may be enough. But body clarifies 3 months. Use body. Might include "Stopped working after just 3 months." with period? continuous substring includes period? Source text: "Stopped working after just 3 months." yes. Evidence span can include period. Better exact continuous substring: "Stopped working after just 3 months." includes trailing period. Fine.

For overheating: "It was overheating very bad" exact substring? Source: "It was overheating very bad and when..." yes.

Could there be claim about durability general: stopped working after 3 months indicates short_lifespan? Taxonomy has reliability_durability: general_durability, stopped_working, intermittent_failure, short_lifespan, cracking_breakage, wear_damage. "Stopped working after just 3 months" primarily stopped_working. Could secondary short_lifespan? But must choose exactly one primary/secondary pair. Which secondary? "stopped_working" is explicit. "short_lifespan" also possible. But review says stopped working. The primary topic reliability_durability, secondary stopped_working. Good.

Potential claim "Don’t recommend" could be other_unknown / uncategorized? But no product attribute. The instruction: "If no supported product claim exists, return empty list." A recommendation is not product claim. Don't include.

Need return JSON with claims array.

Let's craft final exactly. Ensure no extra text. 
{
  "claims": [
    {
      "primary_topic": "reliability_durability",
      "secondary_topic": "stopped_working",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "evidence_span": "Stopped working after just 3 months."
    },
    {
      "primary_topic": "safety_risk",
      "secondary_topic": "overheating",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "evidence_span": "It was overheating very bad"
    }
  ]
}
Check if "overheating" exact span? "It was overheating very bad" yes. Good.

Should title claim also? Maybe if only body stopped working enough. The title "Stopped working after a couple months" is also exact. But including both duplicates not needed. The review has two instances; one claim can cite body. Fine.

Need ensure secondary allowed under primary. safety_risk includes overheating. reliability includes stopped_working. Good.

Potential issue: "It was overheating very bad" grammar but exact. Good.

Potential issue: Overheating is safety_risk? Could be function_performance? Taxonomy has safety_risk overheating, so use that.

Final.

{"claims":[{"primary_topic":"reliability_durability","secondary_topic":"stopped_working","polarity":"negative","evidence_span":"Stopped working after just 3 months."},{"primary_topic":"safety_risk","secondary_topic":"overheating","polarity":"negative","evidence_span":"It was overheating very bad"}]}
